But the governor’s share of border spending has also ballooned since Abbott took office over a decade ago. State lawmakers allotted his office nearly $230 million last year to distribute through grants, largely to local prosecutors and government agencies helping the state with Operation Lone Star.
Though the situation on the ground has changed, one aspect of the emergency declaration has remained constant: the ability of state agencies to award noncompetitive contracts.
DPS and the Texas Military Department have awarded at least six noncompetitive contracts so far during the second Trump administration for work related to the operation where they cite an emergency. This includes a more than $2 million contract to Texas-based CTC Gunworks LLC for rifles and pistols for active-duty personnel. CTC Gunworks officials could not be reached for comment.
Officials with the Texas Military Department referred questions about its procurement process to the governor’s office. A DPS spokesperson said in a written statement that even though the disaster declaration allows for expedited purchases, the department still follows best practices and “aims to select vendors offering the best value, determined by cost, quality, and ability to meet the specific disaster response requirements.”
Regarding the specific contracts, the DPS spokesperson said they were purchases tied to existing state contracts.
The continued funding and expansion of Operation Lone Star has come even as it’s been plagued with problems. In 2022, an investigation by ProPublica, the Tribune and The Marshall Project found that the state’s reported success included arrests unrelated to the border or immigration and counted drug seizures made by troopers from across the state who were not directly assigned to the operation. The Tribune and Army Times also exposed poor working conditions, pay delays and suicides among National Guard members deployed as part of Operation Lone Star.
During a Tribune-hosted event this week with state lawmakers from El Paso, Democratic state Rep. Mary González, vice chair of the Appropriations Committee, said state legislators have already started to scale back when it comes to border funding and there’s interest from both sides of the aisle to continue to do so in the upcoming legislative session.
“I think that the problem is that some of that border security money still lies in the governor’s office which has no checks and balances and because we are still under an emergency — which is not an emergency anymore — an emergency border security statement which he can just use that money, you have seen some questionable appropriations under the veil of border security,” she said.
Abbott, however, has repeatedly said that Texas’ work in securing the border is not over.
“We must secure the border not just for the next two years of the Trump administration, but we gotta do it forever,” Abbott said at a press conference in early October where he discussed the federal government’s $7.5 billion reimbursement for border security expenses the state had incurred.
Rottinghaus said that Texas will always have to confront border crossings and drug trafficking, but the existence of those problems don’t always justify an emergency declaration.
“Even someone who strongly supports the governor’s board of policies might ask whether they want a future governor of the opposite party using the same interpretation of emergency authority for years,” Rottinghaus said, adding that the issue is that “governors, once they get a power, are hesitant to give it back.”

propublica.org.title: Frustrated by Losses in the Courts, Missouri Republicans Want to Change How Top Judges Are Selected
propublica.org.text:
Some 86 years ago, Missouri voters enshrined a system for selecting top judges that would remove political influence from the courts. And almost immediately, it came under attack.
Under what has come to be known as the Missouri Plan, lawyers help choose a slate of three candidates from which the governor must make an appointment for the state Supreme Court, appeals courts and, in some populous areas, the circuit courts.
In the first years after adoption, it faced pushback from party bosses who had historically used judicial seats for political patronage. They said it gave too much power to the lawyers. Voters, though, decisively defeated a repeal measure in 1942.
More recently, the conservative activist Leonard Leo, who viewed Missouri as a crucial battleground, tried in 2007 to persuade Republican Gov. Matt Blunt to reject a slate of Supreme Court candidates — part of a broader effort to weaken a judicial selection system that had become a model for some two dozen states around the country.
Blunt resisted and picked one of the three judges from the approved slate.
Then, in 2012, GOP lawmakers put a proposed overhaul before voters that, if approved, would have given the governor more control. Voters, by a 3-to-1 margin, turned back the plan.
Now the attacks are back, driven by a new grievance.
At President Donald Trump’s behest, Republican lawmakers redrew the state’s congressional map in a mid-decade gerrymander. The goal: to give the GOP a shot at winning seven of Missouri’s congressional seats, instead of the six it now holds.
But voters gathered enough signatures to force a referendum on the map and put it on hold. While Secretary of State Denny Hoskins tried to keep the referendum off the ballot, the Missouri Supreme Court overruled him. It ordered the old map restored until voters decide on the new one.
Hoskins, citing a federal court ruling that contradicted the state’s highest court, directed officials to use the new map anyway, prompting Chief Justice Brent Powell to demand that Hoskins appear in court to show why he shouldn’t be held in contempt.
Fourteen Republican lawmakers responded by threatening to impeach “responsible members of this Court” for “willful neglect of duty, incompetency and misconduct” if the justices held Hoskins in contempt; the court did so anyway. Hoskins backed down and instructed local election officials to distribute ballots using the old map; the justices decided not to have him arrested.
The drama played out as Republicans in Missouri and elected officials nationwide have sought to weaken institutions that limit their power. In North Carolina, the Republican-dominated General Assembly stripped authority from Democratic governors. In Wisconsin, Republicans threatened to impeach a newly elected Supreme Court justice to protect gerrymandered maps. And in New York, Democrats bypassed an independent commission to pass a gerrymander that favored them, but the state’s highest court struck it down.
Rather than electing top judges, as Illinois does, or giving the governor primary responsibility for choosing them, like California, Missouri selects its appellate and Supreme Court judges through a commission made up of three lawyers, one elected by lawyers in each appellate district; three non-lawyers appointed by the governor, one from each district; and a state Supreme Court judge selected by the court. After they are appointed, judges face a retention vote at the first general election after completing one year in office, then every 12 years, with voters deciding whether they keep their positions.
In response to the controversy, a number of Missouri Republicans have attacked the system. U.S. Rep. Jason Smith called for the state to switch to electing its Supreme Court judges. Republican Party executive director Miles Ross declared on X, “The Missouri Plan is done.” Dan Seitz, chief of staff to Sen. Brad Hudson, called for replacing it with a system in which the governor could nominate judges directly, subject to Senate confirmation.
State Rep. Cathy Jo Loy, a Carthage Republican who has introduced legislation in each of the past two sessions to replace the Missouri Plan with gubernatorial appointment and Senate confirmation, said she intends to file a new proposal Dec. 1, the first day lawmakers can file bills for next year’s session. Loy said her opposition to the system predates the recent clashes with the Supreme Court. But she acknowledged that those defeats could give the proposal new momentum.
“There will probably be more appetite because there are several senators that feel the same way,” she said.
Republicans, who hold every statewide elected office, supermajorities in both chambers of the legislature and six of the state’s eight congressional seats, seem to have suddenly found the limits of their power. At the ballot box, voters have overwhelmingly rejected major pieces of the party’s agenda, including an effort to weaken their power to bypass the legislature by amending the constitution or putting laws passed by lawmakers to a statewide vote.
Time and again, when elected officials have sought to limit voters’ use of the ballot initiative, the courts have protected voters’ use of direct democracy. Courts repeatedly rewrote ballot summaries prepared by Republican state officials that they found unfair or misleading, including language describing the initiative that ultimately established abortion rights in 2024.
By the end of that year, after the Missouri Supreme Court rejected a last-minute effort by Republican lawmakers and anti-abortion activists to keep the abortion measure off the ballot, Senate President Pro Tem Cindy O’Laughlin was calling to repeal the Missouri Plan. She proposed replacing the system for selecting Supreme Court and appellate judges with a nonpartisan election. But her bill stalled in committee.
Then came Hoskins. The former state representative and senator from west-central Missouri took office as secretary of state in January 2025 and brought a more combative approach to overseeing elections and ballot measures. Hoskins made a bright-red sport coat his sartorial trademark, often posing with a wood baseball bat and speaking about politics as a series of battles and himself as a conservative warrior.
Hoskins didn’t respond to questions sent to his office. He has previously said that he disagreed with any suggestion that he and Republican leaders were defying the will of voters. He hasn’t publicly called for changing how Missouri selects Supreme Court judges, but his office’s official X social media account reposted Smith’s message calling for the end of the Missouri Plan.
Gov. Mike Kehoe also complained, saying in a post on X that “unelected judges” have shown a “lack of respect for the legislative process.” On a radio show the next day, Kehoe acknowledged that changing how judges are selected hadn’t even been on his radar before the ruling.
“But I think it’s definitely something a lot of people are going to start asking about,” he said. “And I’m not sure the judges across our state, whether Supreme Court or other judges, really wanted that on people’s radar screen.”
Kehoe’s office said it would not respond to questions from ProPublica.
Although some Republicans have derided the state Supreme Court as being a bastion of liberal activists, five of the Supreme Court’s seven judges were appointed by Republican governors. Among them is Powell, whom the then-chair of the state GOP hailed as a “good conservative” before Republican Gov. Eric Greitens selected him in 2017.
Powell, who also serves as chair of the judicial selection commission, declined to comment for this story. In remarks on Sept. 17 to the joint annual meeting of the Missouri Bar and the Judicial Conference of Missouri, he warned of “threats from those who seek to detract from the ideals of our republic and to undermine faith in our sacred institutions — including our legal profession and our courts.”
“It is incumbent on all of us as lawyers and judges to rise up and defend our constitutions and the rule of law,” he added.
Whether there’s enough support to repeal the Missouri Plan remains to be seen. Peverill Squire, a professor emeritus of political science at the University of Missouri, said some of the bills that would eliminate the Missouri Plan might go to committee hearings, “but my guess is there probably won’t be enough appetite among enough Republicans to really want to put it on the ballot.”
Any change would ultimately have to be approved by the voters, something Loy acknowledged could be difficult after Republicans’ recent losses at the ballot box.
But the renewed calls have also mobilized the system’s longtime defenders. Ed Dowd, a former U.S. attorney who for two decades has helped lead the Citizens for Missouri Courts, a campaign that advocates for preserving the Missouri Plan, said the group has historically become most active when the system is under threat.
Dowd’s St. Louis-based firm, Dowd Bennett, recently contributed $100,000 to the campaign.
“It’s something that we take very, very seriously and don’t want to take any chances on losing something that we have that works so well,” he said.

theintercept.com.title: Mother Sues ICE Contractor for Jailing Her and Her Baby in a Hotel Room
theintercept.com.text:
This story was reported and produced by Injustice Watch, a nonprofit newsroom in Chicago that investigates issues of equity and justice in the court system. Sign up here to get their weekly newsletter.
After being detained for five days in an airport hotel, a mother filed suit against a longtime Immigration and Customs Enforcement contractor on behalf of herself and her now 23-month-old son, alleging false imprisonment among other counts.
The lawsuit was filed on September 29, more than a year after an investigation by Injustice Watch and The Intercept revealed MVM Inc. had confined Valentina Galvis, an asylum-seeker from Colombia, and her then seven-month-old infant, a U.S. citizen, in a room at the Sonesta Chicago O’Hare Airport Rosemont last summer. In that reporting, Galvis had described her captivity in stark terms, detailing how she and her son were locked in a room with no way to communicate with the outside world and no idea when, if ever, they would be set free.
Galvis is seeking monetary damages for the alleged harm and injury she and her child suffered as a result of the detention following their arrest by ICE at a Chicago immigration court in June 2025. Galvis named the Sonesta International Hotels Corporation and affiliated companies that own and operate the hotel as defendants in the complaint.
The lawsuit also named five Sonesta and two MVM executives and employees. It identifies JoAnna Granado as the MVM employee who transported Galvis and her son from the hotel to a federal office in Chicago on the day they were released, drawing on the original reporting in which Granado confirmed she was involved in the family’s detention.
Granado and other individuals named in the suit couldn’t be reached for comment. MVM didn’t respond to questions about the lawsuit. During the original investigation, Sonesta said that it “does not condone illegal behavior of any kind” at its hotels. The company declined to comment on the lawsuit.
The suit accused both the ICE contractor and the hotel of detaining Galvis and her child for profit, and alleged the companies engaged in a civil conspiracy by working together to use the hotel room as a detention cell.
“MVM, a federal contractor, physically seized, transported, and confined Ms. Galvis and her infant son,” the suit claimed. “Sonesta knowingly provided and maintained the hotel room used as a makeshift detention cell, profiting from the arrangement while a mother and her infant were locked inside.”
The suit seeks more than $50,000 in compensatory damages, plus punitive damages, and demands a jury trial.
In the complaint, Galvis alleged that her detention at MVM’s hands caused her and her baby a range of physical, emotional, and caregiving harm. Her son had just recently started transitioning to solid foods before the pair were seized by ICE; the suit alleged the infant was provided only scraps of food that were nutritionally inadequate for his age. Meanwhile, confinement-induced stress caused Galvis to decrease her breastmilk production at a time when her son needed it most.
Her baby suffered sleep disturbance and a worsening skin condition, the lawsuit claimed. While MVM had given Galvis an adequate change of clothing, the garments provided for her baby didn’t fit him. Because no laundry service was available, Galvis “washed [the infant’s] clothing in the bathroom sink multiple times,” she stated in an affidavit filed with the court, hanging “the wet clothes near the bed where the air conditioning would dry them quickly.” The infant wore only diapers while his clothes were being washed, and left the hotel on a Tuesday wearing the same outfit he’d worn since he and Galvis were detained by ICE the previous Thursday, according to the affidavit.
In court documents, Galvis alleged MVM confined her and her infant to a room near O’Hare International Airport. Galvis said she was sometimes told she would be taken to a Texas detention center and, on one occasion, that she would be deported to Colombia. She was released by MVM after a federal judge ordered that Galvis and her baby couldn’t be removed from Illinois.
The practice of using hotel rooms as makeshift detention sites has drawn little media attention; far more scrutiny has centered on conditions inside the growing network of ICE detention centers around the country. An inspector general’s report published last month found that ICE had failed to manage its detention space contracts. When asked about it at a September 30 press conference, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended facility conditions, saying detention centers meet and often exceed federal standards — and that comfort isn’t the department’s priority.
“We’re not providing Holiday Inns,” said Mullin.
While ICE agents don’t generally place people in hotels, the agency contracts with MVM to transport immigrant children and families; the contractor sometimes places them in hotel rooms across the U.S. Since fiscal year 2020, MVM has received more than $1.3 billion in ICE contracts, much of it for transporting families.
The lawsuit doesn’t name the federal government as a defendant.
William G. McLean III, who represents Galvis and her baby, underscored the companies’ role in their confinement. “The corporate defendants in this case unlawfully imprisoned and permanently traumatized my clients,” he said, “over five terrifying days after the Department of Homeland Security illegally arrested them.”
Galvis remains at risk of deportation — a final decision on her asylum claim is still pending in immigration court. She’s currently in therapy after an evaluation determined she’s experiencing post-traumatic stress disorder resulting from the detention.
“I isolate myself to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened. I stay home and I do not go outside unless I really need to,” she said in an affidavit.
“Even now, when I go out, I get very nervous, and I feel terror.”
IT’S EVEN WORSE THAN WE THOUGHT.
What we’re seeing right now from Donald Trump is a full-on authoritarian takeover of the U.S. government.
This is not hyperbole.
Court orders are being ignored. MAGA loyalists have been put in charge of the military and federal law enforcement agencies. The Department of Government Efficiency has stripped Congress of its power of the purse. News outlets that challenge Trump have been banished or put under investigation.
Yet far too many are still covering Trump’s assault on democracy like politics as usual, with flattering headlines describing Trump as “unconventional,” “testing the boundaries,” and “aggressively flexing power.”
The Intercept has long covered authoritarian governments, billionaire oligarchs, and backsliding democracies around the world. We understand the challenge we face in Trump and the vital importance of press freedom in defending democracy.
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?
IT’S BEEN A DEVASTATING year for journalism — the worst in modern U.S. history.
We have a president with utter contempt for truth aggressively using the government’s full powers to dismantle the free press. Corporate news outlets have cowered, becoming accessories in Trump’s project to create a post-truth America. Right-wing billionaires have pounced, buying up media organizations and rebuilding the information environment to their liking.
In this most perilous moment for democracy, The Intercept is fighting back. But to do so effectively, we need to grow.
That’s where you come in. Will you help us expand our reporting capacity in time to hit the ground running in 2026?
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?

theintercept.com.title: Reflecting on the Trump Era
theintercept.com.text:
An Iconic Transformation
It was dark and cold when I first spotted him, sitting serenely, bathed in soft light. The statue of Abraham Lincoln at his memorial in Washington, D.C., sits 19 feet tall and weighs 120 tons — a white marble monument dedicated to one of the nation’s most intelligent, eloquent, and moral presidents.
I hadn’t come to gaze upon Lincoln but at the reflecting pool that bears his name. It’s been transformed into a different kind of landmark by the inane, inarticulate, and completely immoral man who now holds that same office Lincoln did.
President Donald Trump wants to remake the landscape of Washington D.C., tearing down the East Wing of the White House to build a monstrosity of a ballroom; adding his name to the Kennedy Center or demolishing it if he can’t; and installing a 250-foot-tall “Triumphal Arch” that will “house … large numbers of drones, plus snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas.” This past weekend, the administration even defied a judge’s order and ripped up 430 mature trees at East Potomac Golf Links, a municipal course in southeastern Washington that Trump wants to refashion into a championship-level course, like those of his personal properties.
Trump’s rehabilitation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — planned to be complete for the nation’s 250th birthday on July 4 — should have been the easiest lift of his planned remodel of the nation’s capital. But it quickly became a monument to failure.
Back in April, Trump said adding a bargain-priced “industrial-grade swimming pool topping” in “American flag blue” to the reflecting pool would leave it looking “gorgeous, beautiful” and would “last for 40 or 50 years.” Instead, the renovation — awarded via a no-bid contract and announced as America 250 festivities on the National Mall approached — started to fail within days. This was followed by a bright green algae bloom and finally a catastrophic lining failure that saw Trump’s chosen coating blister, peel, and then separate from the concrete.
When I visited, the only water in the iconic national landmark — which Martin Luther King Jr. overlooked as he made his historic 1963 “I Have a Dream” speech — was a stagnant puddle that stretched out toward a mass of rotting leaves, a motley collection of plastic beverage bottles, a silver-and-blue aluminum can of RAIN spring water, and a pair of heavy-duty spray bottles often used for commercial cleaning chemicals.
Nested Failures
What I witnessed was emblematic of a White House far out of its depth and completely overwhelmed by disasters — large and small — of its own making. From Washington, D.C., to the Middle East, the Trump administration has been humiliated. It’s a disaster wrapped in fiascos inside a swirling catastrophe, to riff off Winston Churchill’s famed line. These nested failures are legion. The attack on the elementary school in Minab — which killed more than 150 people, most of them children — within the larger failure of the Iran war. The extrajudicial executions of defenseless, shipwrecked survivors within the murderous boat strike campaign. The killings of unarmed people by federal immigration agents and deaths in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody during the larger administration project of anti-immigrant cruelty.
The brutal deportation operations have spawned endless wrongdoing: military occupations of American cities; the arrest and detention of American citizens, the heartless expulsions to third countries; the shootings and beatings of protesters and immigrants, the targeting of Kilmar Abrego Garcia; the swirl of corruption allegations around then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem; and on and on.
Then there is the debasing of democracy and the undercutting of the rule of law through politicization and weaponization of the Justice Department; turning federal law enforcement into a presidential goon squad; gutting of civil rights protections; targeting of political opponents; relentless attacks on the independent judiciary; executive overreach; and the pardoning or commuting of the prison sentences of insurrectionists.
Other scandals and revelations of wrongdoing have been legion: the failure to release the full Epstein files; the settling of Trump’s lawsuit against the IRS; the floating of the “anti-weaponization” fund; the cover-up of the U.S. death toll of the Iran war; Signal-gate; the $400 million Qatari jumbo jet that turned into a security liability; crypto-grifting; quid pro quo tariff reductions; brazen self-dealing; and reckless actions of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, which could result in more than 14 million preventable deaths globally by 2030 — including approximately 4.5 million deaths of children under 5 — all to save Americans about 17 cents per day.
A Presidential Crime Scene
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — dry and barren behind a bevy of barricades — looked to me like an open-air prison. At its head, the west end by the Lincoln Memorial, several black metal crowd-control fences and a similar lone orange metal barrier guarded two layers of chain-link fencing. The rest of the perimeter was hidden behind a single layer of metal fencing supplied by National Rent-A-Fence.
Some of the fencing — which stretched a little less than a mile — was covered in a dark mesh screen that hid the waterless pool. In other areas, the fabric had fallen or was torn down and lay in unsightly heaps. Closer to the east end, one small section of fence lay on the ground — a crumpled mess of metal mesh, poles akimbo, looking like a victim at a crime scene — behind a wall of yellow tape: 27 crisscrossed strands reading “POLICE LINE DO NOT CROSS.” Beyond that, where the water should have been reflecting the rays of the rising sun, pickup trucks rolled through and workers slowly paced, nodded their heads, and stared out on the hardscape, as if waiting for a factory whistle to sound.
In the face of this fiasco, Trump — as always playing the victim and blaming perceived enemies for his shortcomings — has repeatedly claimed knife-wielding vandals slashed the pool’s liner. Several people, including former Olympian David Hearn, were arrested and charged with felonies and misdemeanors, but those cases fell apart. The Interior Department provided documents to the U.S. attorney’s office “indicating that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in June 2026 was the result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings.” The Justice Department also called it a “rushed and botched installation” and in July dropped charges that it had brought against people accused of vandalizing the monument. On October 1, a judge said federal prosecutors cannot refile charges against Hearn. But just last week, Trump was still pushing the lies. “We had vandalism there,” he told the press. “Only sick people do that, and we have their pictures.”
Not far from Lincoln’s statue, the administration offered up these same excuses, complete with Trump’s “filthy dirty” language and vandalism falsehoods. A lone laminated sheet of paper affixed to the fencing read:
The National Park Service staff and contractors are repairing areas damaged by vandals and completing a historic effort to clean, fix, and beautify the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. Since 1922, prior administrations have neglected this iconic national landmark, evidenced most recently by more than half of the pool’s pipes being clogged and the sidewalks and granite coping stones being filthy dirty. The Reflecting Pool will remain drained while this work proceeds so that it can truly reflect the beauty, dignity, and grandeur of our nation’s capital.
Last week, Atlantic Industrial Coatings announced on its website that: “All warranty repairs were completed Friday, 10/2/2026!” The company added: “It has been an honor to serve our great nation!” Trump followed by claiming that the reflecting pool re-do was nearly finished. “I think they’re gonna fill it up this week,” he said on October 6. “The Reflecting Pool is totally complete.”
The National Park Service did not respond to numerous detailed questions from The Intercept about the work by Atlantic Industrial Coatings and whether the pipes were completely unclogged and the granite completely clean. Atlantic Industrial Coatings also failed to respond to questions.
On Monday, a new sign appeared on the fencing as water began flowing back into pool. “The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is being refilled as the National Park Service and contractors put the final touches on a historic effort to clean, repair, and beautify this iconic national landmark,” read a sign without any attribution. It also contained a caveat: “As part of the normal refilling process, the water may temporarily appear cloudy before clearing.”
Whether the Reflecting Pool will again stand as a fitting reflection of “the beauty, dignity, and grandeur of our nation’s capital,” or suffer another catastrophe that leaves it looking like an eyesore, it is symptomatic of the larger issue of unforced errors heaped upon failures which the Trump administration is powerless to fix and can only sometimes, after multiple attempts, contain. It has become a pitiful, helpless giant, unable to achieve even its most modest goals with the power to do little more than spew out misinformation; cloak misdeeds in secrecy; undermine, sabotage, and destroy government institutions; and unleash pain on the most vulnerable and defenseless, like school children in Iran and undocumented immigrants in America.
With Malice Toward All
Trump promised to drain the “swamp” of Washington corruption but instead supercharged it and managed only to drain the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool of water and the country of any shred of decency.
In late August, Trump took to Truth Social to claim he was “six times more popular than Abraham Lincoln” — a reference to a poll of present-day Republicans, of whom 53 percent said the president they most admire is Trump, compared to 8 percent who named Lincoln. That same month, he ranked himself above Lincoln and all other presidents. It’s somehow fitting that Trump wrecked the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in the same way he has soiled the office Lincoln once held.
Whether Lincoln could have imagined a president as depraved as Trump is unknowable but he did fear, in his own time “something of ill-omen, amongst us … the increasing disregard for law which pervades the country; the growing disposition to substitute the wild and furious passions, in lieu of the sober judgment of Courts.” He couldn’t have anticipated the boat strikes, the term human trafficking victim, or the fact that the U.S. might kill the latter during the former, but in that same 1838 speech — when he was just 28 years old — he understood the perils of such summary executions, noting “when men take it in their heads to day, to hang gamblers, or burn murderers, they should recollect, that, in the confusion usually attending such transactions, they will be as likely to hang or burn someone who is neither a gambler nor a murderer.”
Trump is, however, content to kill without compunction and even recently appeared to invite the nuclear annihilation of Los Angeles and San Diego, although it’s increasingly impossible to divine meaning from Trump’s incoherent ramblings. (He has, though, threatened both cities in the past, deploying troops to LA and threatening to do so in San Diego.) Even Lincoln’s armies — turning to “total war” to end a long, brutal, and costly civil war — did not annihilate the South and decimate its people. And at its close, he sought to “bind up the nation’s wounds” with words Trump would choke on: “With malice toward none; with charity for all.”
Lincoln did not believe that the U.S. could be felled by a foreign power but did foresee the possibility of America sealing its own fate. “If destruction be our lot, we must ourselves be its author and finisher,” he said in that 1838 speech. “As a nation of freemen, we must live through all time, or die by suicide.” The reelection of a craven criminal who sought to subvert what remains of democracy in America certainly appears to be more than a mere cry for help.
“Our progress in degeneracy appears to me to be pretty rapid,” Lincoln wrote to his friend Joshua Speed in 1855. Some 171 years later, it may well be complete.
The suffering meted out by Trump has been immense. And his penchant for failure may now be his essential quality. He may ultimately be remembered for turning a reckless military “excursion” into a forever-war failure or as the most debased reprobate to hold the office of the presidency. But Trump’s micro-mismanagement of a local construction project that turned a functioning national monument into a fenced-off blight might be his most illustrative disappointment: a small failure of epic proportions and, in some way, a sorry reflection on all Americans.
IT’S EVEN WORSE THAN WE THOUGHT.
What we’re seeing right now from Donald Trump is a full-on authoritarian takeover of the U.S. government.
This is not hyperbole.
Court orders are being ignored. MAGA loyalists have been put in charge of the military and federal law enforcement agencies. The Department of Government Efficiency has stripped Congress of its power of the purse. News outlets that challenge Trump have been banished or put under investigation.
Yet far too many are still covering Trump’s assault on democracy like politics as usual, with flattering headlines describing Trump as “unconventional,” “testing the boundaries,” and “aggressively flexing power.”
The Intercept has long covered authoritarian governments, billionaire oligarchs, and backsliding democracies around the world. We understand the challenge we face in Trump and the vital importance of press freedom in defending democracy.
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?

We have a president with utter contempt for truth aggressively using the government’s full powers to dismantle the free press. Corporate news outlets have cowered, becoming accessories in Trump’s project to create a post-truth America. Right-wing billionaires have pounced, buying up media organizations and rebuilding the information environment to their liking.
In this most perilous moment for democracy, The Intercept is fighting back. But to do so effectively, we need to grow.

lemonde.fr/en.title: What the demand for decent toilets says about the French student protests
lemonde.fr/en.text:
At Rosa Parks High School in the underprivileged Paris suburb of Saint-Denis, Ilyan grabbed the microphone on Friday, October 9. The higher schooler – who, like all of the individuals mentioned by their first name in this story, did not wish to give his last name – wore powder-pink sweatpants and tousled hair. He represented his grade at the assembly of class representatives – part of the government-mandated "high school democracy time" initiated in the wake of France's nationwide student protests. Ilyan, in his last year of high school, hesitated, cleared his throat, then began. "There are more girls than boys in my class, and they find that there are not enough menstrual products in the bathrooms," he said, speaking on behalf of his peers. "There are some at the nurse's office, but they don't dare to ask."
Growing more comfortable as he spoke, he continued. "When we have class on the third floor, we have to run during recess to use the toilets, which are on the ground floor," he explained. He found it "embarrassing" that "there are no doors at the entrance" to the girls' and boys' bathrooms. "We don't need to know what the girls are doing," he suggested. Ilyan then moved on to his class's concerns about Parcoursup, the French higher education application platform.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Italy's Meloni seeks to trademark her voice to fight 'deepfakes'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Letter from Rome
Her voice is known for being hoarse, raspy from smoking, able to deliver a hypnotic staccato of facts before soaring into sharp recriminations or ridiculing her opponents with merciless irony, tinged with the Roman accent she enjoys playing up before crowds. A major acoustic signature of Giorgia Meloni's performance of power, the Italian prime minister's voice is to become a registered trademark.
In early October, the far-right leader who comes from a neo-fascist background began the process of registering her voice with the European Union Intellectual Property Office. Meloni, who has already been the victim of several deepfakes – AI-generated videos using her face and voice in increasingly realistic ways to spread fake news – was assisted by an Italian law firm in filing an application, which, according to the agency's website, remains under review. The application includes a four-second recording in which she repeats twice: "I am Giorgia Meloni."
She is the first high-profile political figure to seek a trademark for her voice, a move previously reserved for artists such as American singer Taylor Swift or actor Matthew McConaughey. The Italian press, following a report by La Repubblica, widely covered the prime minister's initiative, which was presented by the law firm representing her as a potential deterrent to deepfakes.

lemonde.fr/en.title: A new cycling plan for Paris aims for 'zero deaths and zero serious injuries on the road'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
In Paris, according to counts by cycling advocacy groups, seven people died while cycling in the past year. Six of them lost their lives in similar circumstances: They were stopped next to a truck that turned right without seeing them. This was the fate of a 57-year-old woman on Place de la Concorde on September 21, the most recent victim in this tragic list. "Most cycling deaths happen in this same way, which raises the issue of intersection safety," said Socialist mayor of Paris Emmanuel Grégoire when presenting the city's new cycling plan for the current term on Wednesday, October 14. The plan has a budget of €200 million and the goal of "zero deaths and zero serious injuries on the road."
The municipality pledged to make 420 intersections safer by 2032 – with 56 already scheduled to be completed by 2027 – by physically separating car and bicycle traffic, either through permanent infrastructure or so-called "tactical" measures, using inexpensive and quick-to-install black plastic bollards. The first projects will focus on Place de Clichy and Place de Stalingrad, Porte de Gentilly and Porte de Vanves, and the intersection of Boulevard de Magenta and Boulevard de la Chapelle, which was the site of a fatal accident last spring.

lemonde.fr/en.title: 'Trump has many levers to disrupt the midterms, but far fewer means to turn defeat into victory'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Since his defeat to Joe Biden in November 2020, Donald Trump has relentlessly hammered home the story of a "stolen" election, despite dozens of court rulings to the contrary. With just weeks to go before the midterms on November 3, the US president has continued to push this narrative. Only massive fraud, he claims, could cost him the majority in the House of Representatives and the Senate and poison the last two years of his term – a prospect he especially fears.
How far will the institutions allow him to go in challenging a Democratic victory, as predicted by pollsters? While Trump does have many levers to disrupt the election and the period that follows, he has far fewer means to actually turn a loss into a win.
The first obstacle is the Constitution: US elections are administered locally, not federally, and while Congress can set certain parameters, the federal government has very little direct influence. Furthermore, the midterms differ structurally from the presidential election: There is no Electoral College, and the vice president plays no role on January 6. There is, in short, no "red button" that allows a president to invalidate an election.
This vote is shaping up to be the most closely watched in American political history: 1,000 observers trained by the US Department of Justice (DOJ), along with activists and "citizen journalists," will be deployed to ensure operations run smoothly – which, for some, means rooting out any fraud, real or supposed. With an election of this scope, technical issues are almost inevitable, and an army of observers armed with smartphones will produce footage of what will then be denounced as irregularities. Social media will inevitably amplify this.
A malfunctioning machine, delayed ballots, a reporting error at a tense polling station – all are possible events, but do not in themselves constitute fraud. That such incidents might lead to recounts or legal challenges is entirely legitimate. This is where the federal level can come into play, if a local observer contacts the FBI [the US federal police] or a federal prosecutor. However, internal DOJ guidelines recommend avoiding any action that could affect an election before it is certified.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Brazil's evangelicals grow frustrated with the politicization of their faith: 'It's disheartening to see religion used by the far right'

Like his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro (2019-2023), presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who is leading in the race ahead of the second round scheduled for October 25, has relied on influential pastors to maintain his support among evangelicals, who make up 29% of the population, according to a study published on September 23 by the Institute for Religious Studies (ISER) and polling agency Quaest.
But while 69% of evangelicals said they would vote for Flavio Bolsonaro, compared to 25% for left-wing president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, according to a Datafolha poll released on October 8, many worshipers have grown weary of the politicization of their faith. "Many people left their churches [during the presidential elections] in 2018 and 2022, mainly women, because they saw politics causing divisions," said Livia Reis, an anthropologist specializing in religious issues at ISER. According to the joint ISER and Quaest study, 81% of evangelicals opposed political issues being raised during services or religious events during election campaigns.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Marine Le Pen slams push to 'lock in' EU budget before 2027 elections
lemonde.fr/en.text:
French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen on Wednesday, October 14, denounced as undemocratic a push to "lock in" a deal on the EU's long-term budget ahead of key 2027 elections in France and elsewhere.
EU leaders are scrambling to reach a deal on the bloc's next long-term budget before next year, when elections in many member states – including France, where Le Pen is running in the lead – could complicate any grand bargain.
Addressing a news conference in Brussels on the eve of a leaders' summit, Le Pen called the "accelerating timetable" on agreeing the 2028-2034 budget "an attempt to pre-empt and stifle upcoming democratic choices." "We are being asked to accept its lock-in more than a year ahead of time. None of this is serious," she said, adding it would be a "democratic scandal" if a budget were to be adopted before France chooses a president in April and May next year.
She also said she was convinced "a number of leaders" would not adopt the budget before the election, for fear it would be seen as "illegitimate."
Le Pen reiterated her intent to slash the French contribution to the EU budget, with a "strict cap" of €5 billion. She has previously said she wants to use some of that money for cost savings of €140 billion in France.
'Exact opposite' of Macron
The candidate laid out her broader vision for Europe as the "exact opposite" of President Emmanuel Macron's – pulling no punches in her criticism. "He wanted a powerful Europe. Instead, we got a powerless Europe," Le Pen told reporters. "We were supposed to have a Europe of borders. Rather, we got a Europe that is open to the entire world."
If elected, she vowed to oppose any further enlargement of the European Union – a longstanding position. Current candidate countries include Ukraine as well as Albania and Montenegro, with a renewed push to get new members in.
Le Pen took pointed shots at the European Commission, the EU's executive arm, which "constantly overreaches" and should return to being a "secretariat serving" the member states. On climate policy, she proposed part of each country's contribution to the EU budget should be calculated according to their economies' carbon footprint.
The press conference in Brussels came after Le Pen met her European allies from the Patriots group, which habitually gathers its members before the EU leaders' summits.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Famed French glassmaker Duralex has a new owner
lemonde.fr/en.text:
One chapter closes and a new one begins for the Duralex glass factory in La Chapelle-Saint-Mesmin, located in the Loiret department in north-central France. Only two years after its employees took over as a worker cooperative, and four months after it entered judicial receivership – its fifth such case in 20 years – the Orléans commercial court decided on Wednesday, October 14, to transfer ownership to Tomé, a holding company led by entrepreneur Cédric Meston. Meston, in partnership with a consortium of investors, was selected over the Carlesimo group, a foundry operator based in Saint-Étienne.
Of the two industrial offers, Tomé's proposal retained the highest number of jobs, keeping 155 of the 220 employees still on-site. "We are deeply sorry for the 60 or so people who will lose their jobs, but this was the best solution to ensure the company's survival and prevent a chain reaction affecting Duralex's industrial partners. We will do everything we can to make sure the factory never ends up in this situation again," Meston told Le Monde, adding that he was "honored" by the court's decision.

lemonde.fr/en.title: A century after his birth, Michel Foucault still sells
lemonde.fr/en.text:
One century ago, on October 15, 1926, a boy named Paul-Michel was born in Poitiers, France. He was the eldest son of Paul-André Foucault, a surgeon and professor of anatomy, and Anne Malapert, a surgeon's daughter. Theirs was a French provincial bourgeois family, a dynasty of doctors and local dignitaries. Their house in town stood between a former prison, which had since been replaced by a post office, and a private residence. This house was famous at the time: "The sequestered woman of Poitiers" had lived there, locked away by her family, for more than 25 years.
A hundred years later, Michel Foucault is no longer just one of the leading lights of France's intellectual scene from the 1960s to the 1980s. He is a global star, one of the most often-cited philosophers in the world. That is why the centenary of his birth is no ordinary commemoration, but a genuine intellectual explosion. Seminars, conferences and exhibitions are being held across several continents (beginning with "Foucault, An Intellectual Journey at the Collège de France," running until January 15, 2027) and, in France alone, no fewer than 15 books are being published on the man and his work: essays, biographical accounts, new editions, previously unpublished manuscripts. Now is the time to not only take stock of his legacy, but also to shed new light on it.

welt.de.title: Merz erwartet „sehr, sehr schwierige Verhandlungen“ – und wirbt für Aufstockung der Ukraine-Hilfe
welt.de.text: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) hat vor Beginn des EU-Gipfels in Brüssel mit Blick auf ​die künftige Finanzplanung des Staatenbundes seine Haltung untermauert. Die Vorschläge der EU-Kommission seien für die Mitgliedstaaten ⁠finanziell nicht tragbar. „Das kann sich kein Mitgliedsland in der EU leisten“, sagte Merz am Donnerstag. „Wir müssen das gemeinsame Budget gegenüber den Vorschlägen der Kommission deutlich reduzieren.“ Kein Mitgliedsland könne es sich leisten, Beiträge in diesem Umfang zu zahlen. Der aktuelle Entwurf liege 50 Prozent über dem laufenden mittelfristigen Finanzrahmen. Es stünden ⁠daher ​sehr schwierige Verhandlungen bevor. Mit ‌einer schnellen Einigung bei dem Treffen der Staats- und Regierungschefs rechnet der Kanzler nicht. „Ich rechne auch nicht damit, dass wir an diesem Wochenende, in diesen Tagen zu einem Ergebnis kommen“, sagte er. Ein Abschluss bis zum Jahresende sei jedoch wünschenswert. Die Positionen lägen allerdings noch weit auseinander. „Das heißt nicht, dass wir nicht ‌im November und im Dezember dann zu ⁠Lösungen kommen können“, sagte ​Merz und fügte hinzu: „Aber wir sollten für die Ratssitzung im Dezember ein paar ⁠Oberhemden mehr einpacken als üblicherweise.“ „Wir brauchen Einstimmigkeit im Rat, und von dieser Einstimmigkeit sind wir weit entfernt“, sagte Merz kurz vor Beginn des EU-Gipfels am Donnerstag in Brüssel. Als europäische Prioritäten nannte Merz Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Verteidigung, bei denen die EU jedoch hinter ihrem Zeitplan zurückliege. Zudem verknüpfte ‌er die Finanzdebatte ⁠mit dem Bürokratieabbau: „Wenn ‌wir es ​nicht schaffen, ⁠die überbordende Bürokratie ​in Europa deutlich zurückzunehmen, dann macht es auch relativ wenig ‌Sinn, ​über Geld zu reden.“ Europa müsse handlungsfähig bleiben und ‌souverän ‌werden. Diesen Auftrag erfülle die EU nach seinem Empfinden derzeit nicht ausreichend. Merz wirbt für Aufstockung der Ukraine-Hilfe Außerdem wirbt Merz für eine weitere Aufstockung der Mittel für die Ukraine. „Ich habe heute Morgen in verschiedenen kleineren Treffen dafür plädiert, dass wir alles tun, um der Ukraine auch über den Winter zu helfen, auch im nächsten Jahr zu helfen“, sagte der CDU-Vorsitzende in Brüssel. „Wir werden hier auch noch einmal die Mittel aufstocken müssen, um der Ukraine wirklich dauerhaft zu helfen.“ Konkreter wurde er nicht. Der ukrainische Finanzminister Serhij Martschenko hatte im September bei einem Besuch in Brüssel erklärt, dass im regulären Haushalt seines Landes für nächstes Jahr 32,6 Milliarden US-Dollar (29,1 Milliarden Euro) fehlten. Die Lücke für die Verteidigungsausgaben bezifferte er auf 45 Milliarden US-Dollar (40,1 Milliarden Euro). Für das laufende Jahr ist die Finanzierung der Ukraine gesichert. Merz sprach sich auch klar gegen eine Überführung eines Teils des in der EU eingefrorenen russischen Vermögens an die USA aus, um es dann als Druckmittel in den Bemühungen um Friedensverhandlungen zu verwenden. Die Vermögenswerte – etwa 210 Milliarden Euro – sollten in Europa bleiben, sagte der Kanzler. „Das ist unsere Angelegenheit und darüber entscheiden wir.“ Zuvor hatte die „Financial Times“ darüber berichtet, dass die Idee der Überführung eines Teils des Vermögens in die USA bei einem Treffen von Regierungsvertretern der USA, der Ukraine und Europa in Miami vorgebracht worden sei. Daran nahmen auch Deutschland, Großbritannien und Frankreich teil. Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj nimmt am Freitag am EU-Gipfel teil. Merz war vergangene Woche in Kiew. „Wir sehen eine immer rücksichtsloser werdende Angriffswelle aus Russland gegen die Ukraine“, sagte er in Brüssel. „Und es bleibt bei meiner festen Überzeugung, dass wir nicht nur die territoriale Integrität der Ukraine verteidigen, sondern wir verteidigen die politische Ordnung Europas, die von Russland hier wirklich in jeder Hinsicht unter Druck gesetzt wird.“

Ohne sie wird sie blind, gerät in Panik und rennt planlos umher“, schrieb Medwedjew auf der Plattform X. Er frage sich, was Selenskyj erwartet habe: Trump sei nicht Scholz. Hintergrund ist  ein Streit zwischen Selenskyj und dem amerikanischen Präsidenten. (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6acfd478f02d3efff477db3f/ukraine-krieg-verlieren-einen-starken-partner-selenskyj-fuehlt-sich-von-trump-verraten.html)  Selenskyj zufolge hatten US-Militärs gedroht, Geheimdienstdaten zurückzuhalten, sollten die Angriffe der Ukraine auf russische Raffinerien nicht aufhören. Doch trotz der zweitägigen ukrainischen Kampfpause seien den Streitkräften US-Frühwarnungen vor anfliegenden ballistischen Raketen vorenthalten worden, kritisierte Selenskyj. Die US-Seite habe dies später als technische Störung bezeichnet. Zudem sei der Satellitendienst Starlink des Tech-Unternehmers und Trump-Unterstützers Elon Musk in der Ukraine gedrosselt worden, was Einsätze an der Front und ukrainische Gegenangriffe auf russisches Gebiet behindert habe. Selenskyj wies jedoch die Darstellung einer Panne zurück: Es sei kein technisches Problem gewesen, sondern Absicht, sagte er. Tech-Milliardär Musk wies eine Verantwortung für jegliche Drosselung seines Satelliteninternetsystems Starlink zurück. Die militärische Version von Starlink, Starshield, werde vom US-Militär und letztlich dessen Oberbefehlshaber Donald Trump kontrolliert, betonte er in einem Beitrag auf X. Später legte er dem ukrainischen Präsidenten Selenskyj den Rücktritt nahe. „Es ist Zeit für Selenskyj zu gehen“, schrieb der Multimilliardär in seinem Onlinedienst X. „Das Massaker geht weiter“, schrieb Musk offensichtlich mit Blick auf den Ukraine-Krieg. Selenskyj kündigte unterdessen an, die Angriffe auf russische Ölraffinerien wieder aufzunehmen. Im Zuge eines Diesel-Lieferabkommens mit Russland hatte US-Präsident Trump eine Waffenruhe beider Kriegsparteien bei Angriffen auf Energieanlagen angekündigt. Trump wollte damit kurz vor den US-Kongresswahlen die Kraftstoffpreise senken, die seit Beginn des Krieges der USA und Israels gegen den Iran im Februar stark gestiegen sind. Russland griff aber dennoch weiter ukrainische Energieanlagen an. Trump hatte am Samstag die ukrainischen Angriffe auf die russische Öl-Infrastruktur scharf kritisiert und die Ablösung Selenskyjs gefordert.

welt.de.title: USA erwägen offenbar Einsatz der „Mutter aller Bomben“ gegen Iran
welt.de.text: Das US-Militär hat einem Medienbericht zufolge für ‌den Fall ​neuer Kämpfe ‌im Iran-Krieg Angriffspläne gegen Energie- ​und Atomanlagen der Islamischen Republik vorbereitet, die auch den Einsatz ​seiner schwersten konventionellen Bombe vorsehen. Dies berichtet  der Sender CNN (verlinkt auf https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/15/politics/us-considering-mother-of-all-bombs-iran)  unter ​Berufung auf mit dem Vorgang vertraute US-Vertreter. Sollte ‌US-Präsident Donald Trump entsprechende Angriffe anordnen, könnte demnach die GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb – auch bekannt als „Mutter aller Bomben“ – abgeworfen werden. Der Einsatz der größten nichtatomaren ⁠Waffe im US-Arsenal würde eine erhebliche Eskalation des Konflikts ‌bedeuten. Den Insidern zufolge gibt es in Militärkreisen jedoch ‌Zweifel, ob sich die strategischen Ziele mit ‌der Bombe ⁠tatsächlich ⁠erreichen lassen. Der etwa zehn Tonnen schwere ‌Sprengsatz wurde im ​Jahr 2003 erstmals getestet. Erstmals eingesetzt haben die US-Streitkräfte ​die ​Bombe im April 2017 im Kampf gegen die Islamisten-Miliz IS ⁠in Afghanistan. Ziel war damals ein Tunnelsystem der Extremisten. Widersprüchliche Berichte in israelischen Medien Zuletzt war die Sorge vor einer erneuten Eskalation im Iran-Krieg gestiegen. Trump dementierte vergangenen Donnerstag, den Iran vor den Kongresswahlen Anfang November angreifen zu wollen. Die US-Regierung führe „konstruktive Gespräche“ mit Teheran, hieß es. Die iranische Führung misstraut Trump hingegen und verweist auch auf Angriffe, als mit den USA verhandelt wurde. Trump und Israels Regierungschef Benjamin Netanjahu sollen vergangene Woche über eine mögliche neue großangelegte Militärkampagne gegen den Iran gesprochen haben, wie das US-Nachrichtenportal „Axios“ berichtete. In israelischen Medien gab es unterdessen widersprüchliche Darstellungen über die Absprachen der beiden Verbündeten. Einem Bericht zufolge soll Washington Israel zu einem Alleingang gegen den Iran gedrängt haben. Der Sender N12 berichtete hingegen, US-Vertreter hätten den Eindruck gewonnen, dass Netanjahu selbst Trump zu neuen Angriffen bewegen wollte. Netanjahu sagte dem Armeesender dagegen, eine militärische Konfrontation käme Israel zum gegenwärtigen Zeitpunkt ungelegen. Er warnte Teheran gleichzeitig davor, Israel anzugreifen. In dem Fall drohe dem Iran eine „unvorstellbare Reaktion“, sagte er dem Sender. Ende Februar hatten die USA und Israel ihren Krieg gegen den Iran begonnen. Der Konflikt ist bis heute ungelöst, die Verhandlungen stecken seit Monaten in der Sackgasse. Eigentlich hatten sich Teheran und Washington im Juni auf ein Rahmenabkommen geeinigt, das den Weg für eine dauerhafte diplomatische Lösung ebnen sollte. Im Mittelpunkt des Konflikts stand zuletzt vor allem die Straße von Hormus.

welt.de.title: Musk weist Verantwortung für Starlink-Drosselung in der Ukraine zurück
welt.de.text: Tech-Milliardär Elon Musk hat die Verantwortung für jegliche Drosselung seines Satelliteninternetsystems Starlink zurückgewiesen. Er teilte am Mittwoch auf der Plattform X mit, die militärische Version von Starlink namens Starshield werde vom US-Militär und letztlich dessen Oberbefehlshaber Donald Trump kontrolliert. Die Nutzung des kommerziellen Dienstes Starlink sei auf zivile oder defensive Aktivitäten beschränkt und dürfe nicht für offensive militärische Aktionen verwendet werden, da dies für ein kommerzielles Unternehmen unangemessen wäre, schrieb Musk weiter. Serhij Beskrestnow, ein Berater des ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj hatte zuvor berichtet, dass SpaceX in der Nacht auf Mittwoch die Geschwindigkeit von auf Drohnen installierten Terminals des Satellitendienstes in der Ukraine gedrosselt habe. „Offensichtlich kann diese Maßnahme kein Zufall sein und hängt mit der aktuellen politischen Lage zusammen“, schrieb Beskrestnow in sozialen Medien. Das Weiße Haus kommentierte die Vorwürfe zunächst nicht. Verbindung reicht nicht, um Drohnen mit Düsenantrieb abzufangen Das ukrainische Militär nutzt das Satelliteninternet unter anderem, um Drohnen bei ihrem Zielanflug fernzusteuern. Diese fliegen in der Regel schneller als 160 Kilometer pro Stunde. Bei gedrosselter Geschwindigkeit der Satellitenverbindung könnte die Verbindung zur Drohne ausfallen. Bis Mittwochabend hätten Drohnenpiloten von verbesserten Verbindungen berichtet. Ein ukrainischer Regierungsvertreter sagte jedoch, dies reiche weiterhin nicht aus, um russische Drohnen mit Düsenantrieb abzufangen. Nötig sei eine vollständige Aufhebung der Beschränkungen. Die militärische Version des Satellitennetzwerks ist für die ukrainische Kriegsführung sowohl bei Angriffen als auch bei der Verteidigung von großer Bedeutung. Das System wird nach Angaben Beskrestnows unter anderem für Langstreckeneinsätze von Drohnen, Abwehrsysteme gegen feindliche Flugkörper und die Logistik an der Front genutzt. Die Einschränkung hatte Sorgen geschürt, US-Präsident Donald Trump könne die Unterstützung der Ukraine auf dem Schlachtfeld reduzieren, um Kiew zu Zugeständnissen an Russland oder die USA zu zwingen.

welt.de.title: „Verlieren einen starken Partner“ – Selenskyj fühlt sich von Trump verraten
welt.de.text:
„Verlieren einen starken Partner“ – Selenskyj fühlt sich von Trump verraten
Stand: 07:25 UhrDauer: 4 Minuten
Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj fühlt sich durch den Diesel-Deal von US-Präsident Donald Trump mit Russland und andere Schritte der US-Führung verraten.

welt.de.title: „Verlieren einen starken Partner“ – Selenskyj fühlt sich von Trump verraten
welt.de.text: Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj fühlt sich durch  den Diesel-Deal von US-Präsident Donald Trump mit Russland (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/plus6ac5f2e9b87614811a357465/sprit-aus-russland-hier-geht-es-nicht-wirklich-um-diesel-was-hinter-trumps-deal-mit-putin-steckt.html)  und andere Schritte der US-Führung verraten. Auf eine entsprechende Frage des britischen Moderators Piers Morgan antwortete Selenskyj während seines Besuchs in London: „In der Tat, ja, unter uns gesagt.“ Zu den Handlungen von Trump sagte er, das sei „nicht die richtige Seite der Geschichte“. Morgan schloss in seine Frage auch Trumps Behauptung ein, dass ein Energie-Waffenstillstand zwischen Russland und der Ukraine vereinbart worden sei. Dem seien russische Bombardements auf ukrainische Energieanlagen gefolgt. Selenskyj sagte, die Lage sei komplizierter als seine Emotionen, es gehe nicht nur um ihn. „Unser Land muss überleben“, sagte er. Trump hatte nach einem Gespräch mit dem russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin auf seiner Plattform Truth Social verkündet, Russland werde umgehend mehr als 300.000 Tonnen Diesel für die USA und den Weltmarkt zur Verfügung stellen. Dafür sollten Sanktionen ausgesetzt werden. „Es ist schade, dass wir einen starken Partner verlieren“, beschrieb Selenskyj seine Reaktion. Die Ukraine könne sich keine Schwäche erlauben. „Wir verkaufen unser Land nicht.“ Es gehe nicht um Business, sondern um das Leben, das eigene Land. Es sei schmerzhaft, wenn Trump nicht ihre Seite wähle, sagte der ukrainische Präsident. Es sei okay, wenn der US-Präsident „in der Mitte“ stünde. „Aber wenn man in der Mitte ist, muss man in der Mitte bleiben.“ Er wisse nicht, wer Trump auf die falsche Seite dränge. „Aber das ist nicht die richtige Seite der Geschichte“, sagte Selenskyj. Am Mittwoch war der ukrainische Präsident für Gespräche mit dem britischen Premier Andy Burnham nach London gereist. „Wir schätzen unsere Partnerschaft und setzen unsere Zusammenarbeit für die Sicherheit fort“, lobte Selenskyj auf der Plattform X. Es sei „gerade jetzt besonders wichtig, unsere Luftverteidigung zu stärken und die Ukraine mit allem auszustatten, was sie braucht, um Leben zu schützen“. „Heute wurde beschlossen, die Lieferungen britischer Luftverteidigungssysteme an die Ukraine zu beschleunigen, um gegen antriebsgetriebene ‚Shaheds’ vorzugehen“, ergänzte Selenskyj in seinem X‑Post. „Und ich bin sehr dankbar für diese zeitnahe und dringend benötigte Unterstützung. Ich danke Andy, dem Volk des Vereinigten Königreichs, der Regierung und Seiner Majestät für ihre Solidarität und Unterstützung für unser Land in diesem brutalen russischen Krieg.“

welt.de.title: Trump spricht von Erschießungen wie „in den alten Zeiten üblich“ und sucht Anführer für den Iran
welt.de.text: Wer Informationen zu US-Militäreinsätzen an die Presse durchsticht, sollte nach Meinung von Präsident Donald Trump erschossen werden. Bei einer Wahlkampfveranstaltung im Bundesstaat Arizona echauffierte er sich über einen unbekannten Tippgeber, der die Uhrzeit für Angriffe auf die iranischen Atomanlagen an Journalisten weitergegeben haben soll. „Informanten sollten meiner Meinung nach erschossen werden“, sagte Trump – das sei auch „in den alten Zeiten“ schon üblich gewesen. Die US-Streitkräfte hatten im Juni 2025 im Rahmen der „Operation Midnight Hammer“ die iranischen Uran-Anreicherungsanlagen in Natans und Fordo sowie eine Atomeinrichtung in Isfahan bombardiert. Trump rechtfertigt den damaligen Militäreinsatz – wie überhaupt seinen Krieg gegen den Iran – immer wieder damit, dass die mit dem Verbündeten Israel verfeindete Islamische Republik keine Atombomben haben dürfe. Die Führung in Teheran beteuert stets, das Atomprogramm des Landes diene nur zivilen Zwecken und nicht der Entwicklung von Atomwaffen. Diese Darstellung wird jedoch nicht nur in den USA und Israel bezweifelt. „Ich bin wahrscheinlich ein bisschen zu weit gegangen“ Bei derselben Wahlkampfveranstaltung deutete Trump im Zusammenhang mit dem Iran-Krieg scherzhaft an, zu viele Mitglieder der iranischen Führung getötet zu haben. Er fragte das Publikum spöttisch, ob jemand von den Anwesenden gerne die Führung der Islamischen Republik übernehmen wolle. Bei den gemeinsamen amerikanisch-israelischen Angriffen zu Beginn des Krieges waren Irans Oberster Führer, Ajatollah Ali Chamenei, und große Teile der iranischen Führungsspitze getötet worden. „Also bin ich wahrscheinlich ein bisschen zu weit gegangen. Das tut mir leid, denn ich weiß nicht mehr, mit wem zum Teufel wir es überhaupt noch zu tun haben. Aber das wird sehr bald ein Ende haben“, sagte Trump und befeuerte damit Gerüchte, er werde gleich nach den Wahlen am 3. November den Iran noch einmal mit heftigen Angriffen überziehen.

welt.de.title: Tanker vor Rumänien in Flammen – möglicher Drohnenangriff wird untersucht
welt.de.text: Rumänien untersucht nach eigenen Angaben einen möglichen neuen Drohnenangriff auf einen Tanker vor seiner Schwarzmeerküste. Wie Verteidigungsminister Radu Miruta im Fernsehsender Digi24 sagte, war auf dem unter der Flagge der Komoren fahrenden Schiff „Yara J“ am Mittwochabend ein Brand ausgebrochen. Die Besatzung habe das Feuer selbst löschen können. „Ob es von einer Drohne getroffen wurde oder nicht, wird derzeit untersucht“, fügte er hinzu. Miruta sprach von einem schwerwiegenden Vorfall, der sich in rumänischen Hoheitsgewässern ereignet habe. Das Schiff – laut der Ortungs-Website Vesselfinder ein Tanker für Chemikalien und Ölprodukte – lag nach Angaben des Ministers seit einigen Tagen ohne Fracht vor der rumänischen Stadt Sulina nahe der Grenze zur Ukraine vor Anker. Zwei F-18-Kampfjets aufsteigen lassen Das rumänische Verteidigungsministerium hatte zuvor erklärt, es habe zwei F-18-Kampfflugzeuge aufsteigen lassen, um „eine Gruppe von Luftzielen über dem Schwarzen Meer“ abzufangen. Infolge des russischen Angriffskriegs gegen die Ukraine ist das Schwarze Meer immer wieder Schauplatz von Drohnenvorfällen. Seit der vergangenen Woche trafen mutmaßliche russische Drohnen mehrere Schiffe vor der Küste Rumäniens und des Nachbarlandes Bulgarien.

welt.de.title: „Ich möchte eine Kalaschnikow in die Hand nehmen und auf Juden schießen“
welt.de.text: An diesem Freitag jährt sich der Tod eines der berüchtigtsten Terroristen aller Zeiten zum zweiten Mal. Am 16.10.2024 gelang es israelischen Soldaten im Gazastreifen, Yahya Sinwar zu töten, den Anführer der Terrororganisation Hamas. Seine Eliminierung gilt als großer militärischer und symbolischer Erfolg der israelischen Streitkräfte (IDF). Denn Sinwar war der Haupt-Verantwortliche für das Hamas-Massaker in Israel am 7. Oktober 2023, den größten Massenmord an Juden seit dem Holocaust. Jetzt soll ein offenbar authentischer Brief von Sinwars damals zehnjährigem Sohn Ibrahim verstörende Einblicke in die Erziehungsmethoden des Terror-Chefs ermöglichen. Ibrahim schickte den Brief noch vor dessen Tod an seinen Vater. Der Inhalt zeigt, dass Ibrahim Sinwar von Kindesbeinen an der Hass auf Juden beigebracht wurde. Der Brief liegt WELT exklusiv vor. Darin heißt es wörtlich: „Ich, Ibrahim Im Namen Allahs, des Allerbarmers, des Barmherzigen. Geliebter Vater, ich vermisse dich sehr! Ich möchte dich umarmen und dich siegreich sehen. Ich möchte „Allahu akbar“ (Allah ist am größten) rufen, eine Kalaschnikow in die Hand nehmen und auf Juden schießen. Wann kommst du zurück und schläfst wieder mit mir im Arm?“ Dem Brief sind Zeichnungen von Ibrahim beigefügt. Darauf sind unter anderem ein Panzer mit hebräischen Schriftzeichen, bewaffnete Kämpfer, Raketen und eine offenbar militärische Grenzanlage zu sehen. In dem Brief heißt es weiter: In meiner Freizeit bastle ich Pistolen, Panzer und Kalaschnikows aus Papier und Pappe. Oh Herr, möge der Krieg enden und ich dich wohlbehalten wiedersehen. Möge Allah dich beschützen, Vater. Ich möchte, dass du für mich betest. Friede sei mit dir sowie Allahs Barmherzigkeit und sein Segen.“ Der Brief wurde nach Recherchen von WELT von israelischen Soldaten in einem Gebäude in Rafah gefunden, jenem Ort im südlichen Gazastreifen, in dem Yahya Sinwar getötet wurde. Auf Anfrage von WELT erklärt eine Sprecherin der israelischen Streitkräfte: „Auch zwei Jahre nach der Tötung von Yahya Sinwar prägt die mörderische Ideologie, die er propagierte, weiterhin den Gazastreifen. Der Brief und die Zeichnungen verdeutlichen, wie sich Sinwars mörderische Ideologie in der Erziehung seiner Kinder widerspiegelt. Sie zeigen, welchen Einfluss die von der Hamas propagierten Werte des Hasses und der Gewalt auf die junge Generation im Gazastreifen haben.“ Der bekannte Islamismus-Experte und Buchautor Ahmad Mansour hält den Brief für authentisch. Mansour ist selbst arabisch-palästinensischer Herkunft und erklärt gegenüber WELT: „Das entspricht nicht nur den Erziehungsmethoden der Hamas, sondern ist auch in Teilen der palästinensischen Gesellschaft, insbesondere im Gazastreifen, tief verankert. Der Hass auf Juden – wohlgemerkt: Er spricht nicht von Israelis, sondern von Juden – und die Tötung von Juden wird so lange normalisiert, bis selbst kleine Kinder davon träumen.“ Auch Professor Danny Orbach, Militärhistoriker an der Hebräischen Universität Jerusalem, ist „nahezu sicher“, dass der Brief echt ist. Seine Einschätzung: „Der Brief zeigt deutlich den bizarren Todeskult unter den Hamas-Führern, den überzeugten Hamas-Aktivisten und ihren Familien.“ Wie WELT bei Recherchen im Gazastreifen erfuhr, rekrutiert die Hamas, die durch Israels Kampf gegen den Terror geschwächt ist, inzwischen auch Minderjährige. Islamistische Gewaltideologie und Judenhass sind im Gazastreifen sogar schon in der Gedankenwelt von Kindern ausgeprägt. Das belegen auch Augenzeugenberichte vom 7. Oktober 2023. Alon Gat, der gemeinsam mit seiner Frau und seiner dreijährigen Tochter von Hamas-Terroristen entführt wurde, erinnert sich an die Begegnung mit einem Kind, das vom Gazastreifen aus in den Kibbuz Be´eri gelaufen war, um zu plündern: „Der Junge war etwa zwölf Jahre alt. Ich bin mir sicher, dass er zuvor die Leichen gesehen hatte. Er sah mich und meine Tochter an, und ich sah ihn an. Und ich konnte in seinen Augen keinerlei Mitgefühl erkennen. Die Menschen waren ihm völlig egal.“ Jan Philipp Burgard (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/autor/jan-philipp-burgard/)  ist Axel Springer Global Reporter für den Nahen Osten.

welt.de.title: „Ein Volk, das hungert, geht auf die Barrikaden“ – Jetzt zeigt sich, wie verletzlich unsere Systeme sind
welt.de.text: In einem beispiellosen Angriff legen Hacker in 500 Supermärkten in Frankreich die Kühlschränke lahm. Die Folgen sind auch Tage später noch zu spüren. Experten äußern einen beunruhigenden Verdacht.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Bugünden itibaren 3 burcun hayatı sil baştan değişecek: Plüton resti çekti, devir değişiyor
sozcu.com.tr.text: 16 Ekim Cuma günü Plüton'un düz hareketine geçmesiyle birlikte, 3 burç için son derece güçlü ve yepyeni bir dönem başlıyor. Astrolojide Plüton'un ileri hareketi, tıkanan işlerin hızla çözüme kavuşmasını ve hayatın ritminin hızlanmasını sağlar. Bu geçiş sadece derin bir dönüşümü değil; aynı zamanda hedeflerimize sadık kalma ve hayallerimizi gerçeğe dönüştürme gücünü de beraberinde getirir. Plüton, kendimize verdiğimiz sözleri tutmamız için bizi adeta meydan okumaya davet ediyor. Eğer kendinize başarı, değişim veya ilerleme sözü verdiyseniz, işte bunu somutlaştırmanın tam zamanı... Bu güçlü kozmik döngüde emeklerinizin karşılığını net bir şekilde görecek, attığınız adımlarla kendinizle gurur duyacaksınız. İşte bu güçlü dönüşümden en çok etkilenecek ve yeni bir döneme adım atacak 3 burç... 1. Oğlak Burcu "Artık vakit kaybetmek yok, şimdi tam anlamıyla işe koyulma zamanı!" Cuma günü, Plüton’un düz hareketiyle birlikte içinizde bambaşka bir ilham ve motivasyon dalgası hissedeceksiniz. Bu kozmik enerji, hayatınıza tatlı bir aciliyet duygusu katarak ertelediğiniz ne varsa hemen şu an harekete geçmeniz için sizi yüreklendirecek. Bir Oğlak olarak bu dönemde mükemmelliğe ulaşma arzunuz zirveye çıkıyor. Hayatınızda somut ilerlemeler kaydetmekten ve geleceğe yönelik büyük adımlar atmaktan büyük keyif alacaksınız. Ancak hedeflerinize ulaşmak için bazı radikal değişiklikler yapmanız gerektiğinin de farkındasınız. Hayatınızı daha iyi bir noktaya taşımak istiyorsanız, her şeyi olduğu gibi bırakamazsınız. Neyse ki bir "kaptan" edasıyla yapılması gerekeni korkusuzca yapmak tam da sizin prensibiniz! 2. Akrep Burcu "Hayatınızın direksiyonuna geçin ve ipleri elinize alın." Burcunuzun yönetici gezegeni olan Plüton’un ileri hareketi, Cuma günü size aradığınız o güçlü motivasyonu fazlasıyla sunacak. Bu süreç, daha önce hiç denemediğiniz yöntemlerle hayatınızın kontrolünü tamamen elinize almanızı sağlayacak. Son zamanlarda hayatınızın bazı alanlarında disiplini elden bıraktığınızı ve işlerin yavaş yavaş kaosa sürüklendiğini fark etmiş olabilirsiniz. Ancak bu durumun böyle devam etmeyeceğini en iyi siz biliyorsunuz. Hayatınızı yeniden düzene sokacak olan kişi sadece sizsiniz; çünkü bu sizin hayatınız ve kimse sizin yerinize bu adımı atmayacak. Cuma günü itibarıyla ciddiyeti eline alma ve öz disiplini devreye sokma vakti. Sizi bekleyen bu güçlü yeni dönemi en verimli şekilde değerlendirmek için sabırsızlanacaksınız. 3. Koç Burcu "Sınırlarınızı yeniden çizin ve hayatınızın kontrolünü geri kazanın." Kendinizi güvensiz hissettiğiniz ya da sınırlarınızın tehdit edildiği bir durumun içinde bulduysanız yapmanız gereken tek bir şey var: Konumunuzu ve şartlarınızı hemen değiştirmek! Siz olayları olduğu gibi kabullenip köşesine çekilecek biri asla değilsiniz. Şimdi, o meşhur Koç enerjisiyle harekete geçme zamanı. Başkalarının ne düşündüğünü ya da ne söyleyeceğini bir kenara bırakın. Cuma günü sadece kendi kalbinizin sesini dinleyin; aldığınız kararlarla kendinizi çok daha huzurlu, güvende ve mutlu hissettiğiniz bir noktaya ulaşın. Bu dönüşüm süreci ve Plüton'un bu sert hamlesi elbette kolay olmayacak, ciddi bir çaba gerektirecek, ancak siz Zodyak'ın en güçlü savaşçılarından birisiniz. Bu güçlü yeni dönemi cesaretle kucaklayın, değişimi başlatın ve hayatınızı geri kazanın. Bunu başaracak güç içinizde var.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Eski eşini eşarpla boğan sanığa ağırlaştırılmış müebbet
sozcu.com.tr.text: Olay, 11 Eylül 2025'te saat 01.00 sıralarında Muratpaşa ilçesi Güzeloba Mahallesi Örnekköy Caddesi'ndeki 3 katlı apartmanın giriş katında meydana geldi. Olaydan 1 hafta önce yeni evine taşınan 2 çocuk annesi Hanım Biçer, eski eşi Hızır Çelik ile eve geldi. İkili arasında çıkan tartışma kavgaya dönüştü. Çelik, eski eşi Biçer'i eşarpla boğup ardından yastıkla yüzünü kapattı. Evden 3 saat sonra çıkan Hızır Çelik, yaklaşık 16 saat sonra Hanım Biçer'in kardeşini arayarak, "Eşimi öldürdüm, gidip teslim olacağım" diyerek telefonu kapattı. Biçer'in yakınları, durumu 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi'ne bildirdi. TESLİM OLUP, TUTUKLANDI Eve giren Cinayet Büro Amirliği ekipleri, Hanım Biçer'in hayatını kaybettiğini belirledi. Biçer'in cansız bedeni, Antalya Adli Tıp Kurumu morguna götürüldü. Hızır Çelik de Döşemealtı Polis Merkezi Amirliği'ne gidip teslim oldu. Çelik'in ilk ifadesinde; eşinin kendisine, "Tekrar görüştüğümüzü ailene söylerim" diye tehdit ederek para istediğini, bu nedenle tartışma çıktığını ve öldürdüğünü söylediği belirtildi. Hızır Çelik, işlemleri sonrası tutuklandı. EVE GİRİŞLERİ GÜVENLİK KAMERASINDA Diğer yandan Hanım Biçer'in son anları, güvenlik kamerasına yansıdı. Görüntülerde; Biçer ile Çelik'in siteye girdikleri, Hanım Biçer'in kapıyı açtığı ve ikilinin eve girdiği, bir süre sonra Hızır Çelik'in evden tek başına çıktığı görüldü. Hızır Çelik hakkında 'Kadına ve boşandığı eşe karşı kasten öldürme', 'Kişinin ölmesinden yararlanarak hırsızlık' suçlarından iddianame hazırlandı. SANIK: CİNAYET İŞLEMEDİM Antalya 1'inci Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'nde görülen karar duruşmasına tutuklu sanık Hızır Çelik, müştekiler Resul Biçer ile Recep Biçer ve taraf avukatları katıldı. Son sözü sorulan sanık Hızır Çelik, "Cinayet işlemedim, işlemek isteseydim ilk gün gerçekleştirirdim. Boşandıktan sonra ben kendimi hayat kadını gibi hissedip ona göre yaşıyordum, korktuğum için 6-7 ay öyle yaşamaya çalıştım. Çocuklarıma hem annelik hem babalık yapıyordum. Hanım’ın ailesiyle baş etmek mümkün değil, 'boşanma, öldür' dediler. 8 ay boyunca kaçmaya çalıştım, çocuklarımı korumak için her şeyi yaptım. Birini öldürmek istesem inşaat işi yapıyordum, bir yere götürür öldürürdüm" dedi. Mahkeme heyeti, sanık Hızır Çelik'i ağırlaştırılmış ömür boyu hapse mahkum etti. Sanığın cezasında indirim uygulanmadı. 'VİCDANIMIZ RAHATLADI' Duruşmanın ardından Önce Çocuklar ve Kadınlar Derneği adına açıklama yapan Avukat Yağmur Burçin Sayın Kurt, "Bir önceki celsede mütalaa verilmişti. Mütalaa doğrultusunda haksız tahrik indirimi uygulanmadan emsal niteliğinde bir karar aldık. Bu kararın diğer cinayet dosyalarında da uygulanmasını istiyoruz. Her ne kadar fazlasıyla haksız tahrik indiriminden faydalanmak için maktullere iftiralar atılmış olsa da bu dosyada bunu görmedik. Sanık ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapis cezası aldı. Her ne kadar ölen geri gelmese de vicdanımız rahatladı" dedi.

sozcu.com.tr.title: İstanbul’da sağanak sonrası çatıyı tamir ederken hayatını kaybetti
sozcu.com.tr.text: Zeytinburnu'nda yaşayan Rahmetullah Acar tamir için 3 katlı binanın çatısına çıktı. Tamirat sırasında dengesini kaybeden Rahmetullah A. zemine düştü. Yaralanan Rahmetullah A. kaldırıldığı hastanede tüm müdahalelere rağmen kurtarılamadı. Olay, saat 11.00 sıralarında Yenidoğan Mahallesi 45/2 Sokak'ta meydana geldi. Edinilen bilgiye göre, 3 katlı binanın çatısında sağanak yağmur sonrası tamir yapan Rahmetullah Acar dengesini kaybederek zemine düştü. Acar'ın düştüğünü görenlerin ihbarı üzerine olay yerine sağlık ve polis ekipleri sevk edildi. Ağır yaralandığı belirlenen Acar, sağlık ekiplerinin olay yerindeki ilk müdahalesinin ardından ambulansla hastaneye kaldırıldı. Acar'ın hastanede yapılan tüm müdahalelere rağmen hayatını kaybettiği öğrenildi. İKİNCİ KEZ ÇATIDA TAMİR YAPMIŞ Diğer yandan Rahmetullah Acar'ın sağanak sonrası hasar meydana gelen çatıda dün de tamir için çalıştığı öğrenildi. Devam eden sağanak sonrası bugün ikinci kez çatıya çıkan ve tamirat yapan Acar'ın ölümüyle ilgili soruşturma başlatıldı. İDDİAYA GÖRE AYAĞI KAYDI VE ÇATIDAN DÜŞTÜ Aynı mahallede oturan görgü tanığı Mustafa Güder, "Çatıyı tamir etmek için saat 09.30-10.00 civarlarında oraya çıkmış. Hatta dün 15.30 civarında da iki arkadaşı ve bir kadınla beraber orada çatıyı tamir ediyorlardı. Sanırım olmadı; amca çatıyı tamir etmek için tekrar çıktı. Bir tertibat bir koruma olsaydı iyi olurdu. Adamın ayağı kaydı saat 09.30-10.00 civarlarında düştü. Ambulansla hastaneye kaldırdılar yeni duydum vefat etmiş. Allah rahmet eylesin yakınlarına da sabır versin. Kendisini tanıyorduk biz de üzüldük" dedi.
